rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose adjectival description for food cooked by roasting.

example.english: These are roast chicken wings, not fried ones.
example.traditional: 呢啲雞翼係燒熟咗嘅，唔係炸嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 gai1 jik6 hai6 siu1 suk6 zo2 ge3 m4 hai6 zaa3 ge3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for roasting food with dry heat, including over a fire or in embers.

example.english: We roast chicken wings beside the campfire.
example.traditional: 我哋喺營火旁邊燒雞翼。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hai2 jing4 fo2 pong4 bin1 siu1 gai1 jik6

rows.note: Use this for someone who has been playfully mocked or bantered by others.

example.english: People roast you all the time, so don’t take it so seriously.
example.traditional: 你成日畀人串嘅，唔使咁介意啦。
example.jyutping: nei5 seng4 jat6 bei2 jan4 cyun3 ge3 m4 sai2 gam3 gaai3 ji3 laa1

rows.note: Use this when “roasted” means being harshly scolded or severely criticized rather than playfully teased.

example.english: People roast me whenever I’m late.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ci4 dou3 zau6 bei2 jan4 naau6 ge3

rows.note: Use this when roasting someone means mocking or making cutting fun of them.

example.english: Don’t roast my new hairstyle anymore.
example.traditional: 你唔好再串我個新髮型喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 cyun3 ngo5 go3 san1 faat3 jing4 laa3

rows.note: Use this when someone is being vigorously scolded rather than mocked.

example.english: The teacher gave us a proper roast all through class.
example.traditional: 老師成堂都喺度鬧我哋。
example.jyutping: lou5 si1 seng4 tong4 dou1 hai2 dou6 naau6 ngo5 dei6

rows.note: Use this especially for dry-roasting beans, seeds, or similar food in a pan, rather than for ordinary oven roasting.

example.english: My mum likes to roast peanuts in a wok.
example.traditional: 我阿媽鍾意用鑊炒花生。
example.jyutping: ngo5 aa3 maa1 zung1 ji3 jung6 wok6 caau2 faa1 sang1
